architecture_summary:
The four lenses converge on one structural insight that resolves the two dominant defect classes (invented_terminal_fork and tiny-stub over_split): both are the SAME mechanism at two scales — the medial axis of a near-rectangular cap/serif sprouts diagonal branches toward each convex corner. The textbook discriminator that separates a real feature from a corner artefact is the separation angle (object-angle / theta-medial-axis) of the two boundary contact points that generate each medial pixel: a real serif/limb is bounded by two SEPARATED outline flanks (contacts ~120-180deg apart), a corner branch has both contacts CONVERGING on one vertex (angle -> 0). This is computable for free because core/skeleton.py:57 already calls distance_transform_edt(mask_clean) but discards the return_indices field, and analyze_junctions has no width geometry at all (dist_map is threaded into build_annotated_graph and smooth_and_wobble but never into analyze_junctions — that is precisely why it cannot tell a cap fork from a real Y-junction).

Conflict resolution across lenses: (1) For over_split the python-implementer's "absorb/splice the stub into its parent stroke" is CHOSEN over the medial-axis-theorist's "prune the branch", because the project rule is that moderate serif flicks are APPROVED (Garamond H = stem,stem,crossbar+flicks) — deleting the branch destroys ink coverage and the approved visual, whereas merging it preserves the flick while collapsing the stroke count. Separation-angle pruning at the skeleton stage is reserved ONLY for the flat-CAP corner-fork case (no real ink feature to preserve there); the slab/serif over_split is handled later at chain-cleanup by absorption. (2) The invented_terminal_fork root fix lands at the EARLIEST correct stage (skeleton prune with a separation-angle gate) as primary; the analyze_junctions cap-veto is dropped from initial scope as redundant defence-in-depth (per the implementer's own note — do not build both a prune AND a post-hoc hook remover). (3) The bowl-direction fix is a one-line sign flip (CW->CCW) per all lenses, scoped to closed loops only. (4) The on-ink clip is a deterministic safety net, not a substitute for root cause. (5) Detectors are rewritten around a single shared curve_profile primitive plus a mask-diff coverage detector (font-agnostic, grounded in the artist's own MAT width model) and calibrated by ROC against the 624 labeled examples with GroupKFold-by-font. The first action before any threshold-fitting is to VERIFY the 624 per-(font,char) labels are recoverable as a flat table — both the qa-metrology-engineer and the data on disk (epst_batch_qa.json holds aggregates + ~10 example letters per kind, not 312 per-letter records) flag this as the blocking precondition; if only aggregates exist, fall back to a stratified ~120-letter relabel with Wilson intervals. Total scope is lean: two new skeleton/graph helpers, two short chain-cleanup passes, one sign flip, and a detector-module rewrite that only touches quality/ (cannot regress rendered glyphs). The 51/52 clean script path is structurally protected because every source fix only removes/retangents/merges (never adds strokes) and every gate has r<1.5px and width-relative guards that fall back to current behaviour on thin cursive strokes.

source_fixes.name: Capture EDT nearest-boundary index field (enabling change)
source_fixes.parameters: n_rim=24 (rim samples; fixed). r<1.5px guard (below thinnest hairline at 384px -> protects script strokes). No new magic numbers leak to render scale; all width-relative via dist.
source_fixes.preserves: Pure infrastructure: changes no output by itself. The dist_clean values are unchanged (same EDT); only the previously-discarded index field is now retained. Must keep rng=0 path intact.

source_fixes.name: Separation-angle gate on flat-cap corner branches
targets: invented_terminal_fork (Lato l, r, d, F, u, x, N)
source_fixes.algorithm:
Augment the existing length gate. After computing `threshold` and walking `path` from endpoint ep:

  sep = _separation_angle(ep, dist, mask_clean)
  is_corner = sep < radians(CORNER_SEP_DEG)
  if len(path) < threshold or (is_corner and len(path) < CORNER_LEN_FACTOR*threshold):
      erase path[:-1]

The corner rule ONLY escalates pruning for branches that are already short-ish (len < CORNER_LEN_FACTOR*threshold) AND corner-shaped (contacts converge), so a long legitimate stroke can never be eaten. A flat 90deg cap corner gives sep ~40-90deg at the tip; a serif (a little rectangular protrusion) gives sep ~150-180deg because its disc is squeezed between two near-parallel flanks. Validate the bimodality on Lato (expect ~40deg corner branches vs ~170deg serifs) before trusting the threshold.
source_fixes.parameters: CORNER_SEP_DEG=65 (below this => corner-induced; default conservative). CORNER_LEN_FACTOR=2.0 (cap on how much longer than the length floor a corner branch may be and still be pruned; a corner diagonal cannot exceed ~1x stroke width). Both gated behind `if mask_clean is not None` so older callers degrade to current behaviour. Scales with stroke width through the existing `threshold = max(12, local_thickness*2.2)`.
source_fixes.preserves: Garamond serif flicks (sep stays high -> only the existing length floor applies, unchanged). The r<1.5 guard returns pi (never prunes) on thin cursive strokes -> script 51/52 untouched. Closed loops/curves have no degree-1 spur endpoints here -> untouched. Italic/oblique terminals at intermediate angles bounded by the 2.0x length cap.

source_fixes.name: Width-scaled stub absorption (preserves approved flick behaviour)
source_fixes.pipeline_stage: templates/eulerian.py — new function absorb_stubs, called in trace_glyph_eulerian after build_chains (line 598) and BEFORE _orient_clockwise_if_closed/order_all_walks
targets: over_split (Arvo X=12, m=10, E=10; EBGaramond H=7, W=9)
source_fixes.parameters: STUB_FACTOR=1.2 (chain shorter than 1.2x its own local width is a stub candidate; conservative). NOISE_FACTOR=0.5 (isolated chain below 0.5x width is dropped as skeleton noise). No SPLICE angle gate is required because the host is identified by shared-pixel identity, not tangent continuation — the serif leaves the stem at ~90deg, which is exactly why analyze_junctions refused to pair it and why re-attaching here (at a stage that knows 'this is a tiny tail') is correct. All thresholds width-relative.
source_fixes.preserves: Full-width bars (E's three horizontals span >> local width -> not stubs). Approved Garamond flicks (already attached / above factor). Must run BEFORE orientation/ordering. Requires the junction pixel identity preserved through build_chains (it is — chains store pixel walks). Risk: a condensed E middle bar near threshold — validate on Arvo E; STUB_FACTOR=1.2 is conservative.

source_fixes.name: Closed-loop orientation: clockwise -> counter-clockwise
targets: wrong_direction on closed bowls o, a, d, g, b, p, q
source_fixes.algorithm: Flip the sign test at line 458. In image-y-down coords a positive shoelace (area2>0) is clockwise on screen; standard penmanship draws Latin bowls counter-clockwise. Change `if area2 < 0: walk = walk[::-1]` to `if area2 > 0: walk = walk[::-1]`. Optionally refine the entry point from plain topmost (argmin y) to rightmost-of-top-band (pen enters a roundhand bowl near 1 o'clock): among pixels within ys.min()+1, pick max-x. Keep plain topmost as the safe fallback if the refined entry reads oddly on 'g'. Scoped to truly closed walks (walk[0]==walk[-1]) only.
source_fixes.parameters: No numeric parameters beyond the existing top-band tolerance of 1px. Pure convention flip.
source_fixes.preserves: Open strokes (cursive upstrokes, Z/7 corners, the d/g stems which are SEPARATE open chains) are untouched -> 'd' = bowl(CCW)+stem(top-down) still composes. Script retraces are open chains -> untouched. NOTE: 'c' is an OPEN arc, not caught here — its direction lives in _orient_walk_for_writing and is deliberately left for a separate vision-validated pass (changing open-stroke direction risks the legitimate cursive-upstroke-entry cases). Only vision-QA can ratify the flip; re-render o/a/d/g/b/p/q/e.

source_fixes.name: Direction/order prior refinement (minimal, scoped)
source_fixes.algorithm: Keep the existing print-convention defaults (verticals top-down, horizontals L-R, big-first, dots-last) — they are correct TENDENCIES per the user. Make ONE safety change: in _orient_walk_for_writing, ABSTAIN from forcing top-down on a stroke that is curved (heading std over the walk > 0.25 rad) so legitimate cursive entry upstrokes are not flipped. Do NOT add new ordering rules in this pass; the corrected rules (cursive upstrokes legitimate, retracing legitimate, strict L-R is a tendency not a law) are TENDENCIES the user said should not be hard-enforced, so they are encoded only as scored advisory DETECTORS (see convention_priors detector), not as orientation mutations.
source_fixes.parameters: STRAIGHTNESS_RAD=0.25 (heading-std threshold above which a stroke is 'curved' and exempt from top-down forcing). Width-independent (angular).
source_fixes.preserves: Script font upstrokes (curved -> exempt). All currently-correct print orientations (straight verticals still forced top-down). Lowest-risk change; do not over-reach into open-stroke direction policy.

cleanup_pass.description: Deterministic on-ink clip / overshoot-trim safety net for the residual 6 stray cases (terminal overshoot past the ink edge from junction-merge endpoint extension, and resampling cutting through white space). It is a strict NO-OP on any walk fully inside the mask, so it cannot regress the 51/52 clean script path. This is the secondary net AFTER the root-cause skeleton fixes, not a substitute.
cleanup_pass.algorithm:
def clip_to_ink(walk, mask, dist_map, max_nick_factor=0.75):
    ys = clip([p[0] for p in walk], 0, H-1); xs = clip([p[1] for p in walk], 0, W-1)
    on = mask[ys.astype(int), xs.astype(int)].astype(bool)
    if on.all(): return [walk]              # NO-OP for correct input
    # (a) trim leading/trailing off-ink run (terminal overshoot)
    i0 = first_true(on); i1 = last_true(on)
    walk, on = walk[i0:i1+1], on[i0:i1+1]
    if len(walk) < 2: return []
    # (b) split at any interior off-ink run longer than width-scaled nick
    segs=[]; cur=[walk[0]]; run_px=0.0
    for j in 1..len(walk)-1:
        step = dist(walk[j], walk[j-1]); w = 2*dist_map[round(ys[j]),round(xs[j])]
        if not on[j]:
            run_px += step
            if run_px > max_nick_factor*max(w,3.0):
                if len(cur)>=2: segs.append(cur); cur=[]; run_px=0.0
        else:
            run_px=0.0; cur.append(walk[j])
    if len(cur)>=2: segs.append(cur)
    return [s for s in segs if _polyline_length(s) >= MIN_WALK_LEN_PX]

The medial axis is inside the mask by construction, so ANY off-ink pixel is provably a hygiene/merge artefact (merge_nearby_junctions and collapse_parallel_edges prepend/append node pixels that can sit slightly outside ink). Trimming off-ink ends is always safe; interior SPLIT only fires when the off-ink run exceeds 0.75x local width (a genuine white-space bridge), so a 1-2px junction nick at a sharp corner (Z, 7) is tolerated. Width-scaled, deterministic.
cleanup_pass.placement: templates/eulerian.py::trace_glyph_eulerian, applied per ordered walk immediately BEFORE smooth_and_wobble (line 623 loop): `for w in ordered: for seg in clip_to_ink(w, main_mask, dist): smooth_and_wobble(seg, ...)`. CRITICAL: pass main_mask (the dot-split mask from _split_mask_dots), NOT the raw mask, or i/j stems mis-clip against the tittle-removed mask. max_nick_factor=0.75.

detector_suite.name: curve_profile shared primitive
detector_suite.math: Given (xs,ys), arc-length-uniform resample at ds=0.5px; unwrapped heading theta(s)=atan2(dy,dx); signed curvature kappa(s)=dtheta/ds. Gaussian scale-space smoothing at sigma=0.5*median_width gives kappa_smooth; band-pass = kappa - kappa_smooth.
detector_suite.algorithm: New file core/curves.py: curve_profile(xs,ys,ds=0.5) -> (s, x, y, theta, kappa). Every curvature-based detector is a thin predicate over this one primitive, giving uniform behaviour across open/closed/cornered/cursive curves and one place to calibrate ds and sigma.
detector_suite.calibration: PRECONDITION for all detectors: run on the PRE-WOBBLE centerline (the raw graph walk), because smooth_and_wobble injects OU lateral noise at amplitude 0.18*width that contaminates curvature. Either expose the pre-wobble walk to the cascade or trace with wobble_amp=0 for QA. Also thread dist_map through run_cascade (currently only mask is passed).

detector_suite.name: curvature-spectrum zigzag (replaces broken tortuosity)
detector_suite.replaces: geometric_issues zigzag branch (cascade.py:79, tortuosity=plen/max(disp,1e-6) -> 203 on a perfect 'o' because disp->0)
detector_suite.math: Zigzag is high-frequency OSCILLATION of heading, not a global chord ratio. Two complementary signals: (i) heading-reversal count = number of samples where dot(h[k],h[k-1]) < cos(140deg) — a smooth loop/S-curve turns continuously but NEVER reverses heading, so it scores 0; (ii) scale-space turn density Rdens = integral|kappa-kappa_smooth|ds normalised by arc length in widths, plus a count of significant band-pass alternations.
detector_suite.algorithm: Flag if (alternations >= 3 AND Rdens > 0.8) OR (heading_reversals >= 2). One legitimate fold-back (script retrace) gives 1 reversal -> allowed; a serpentine M-diagonal gives many. Closed bowls never consult displacement -> the 'o' explosion is gone by design. Skip strokes shorter than 3*median_width (too short to oscillate; those are over_split's province).
detector_suite.calibration: Sweep alternation/Rdens/reversal thresholds against labeled zigzag/double_trace positives vs S-curve and closed-loop negatives. Target: 0/6 stray-as-zigzag, 0 bowls flagged. F-beta=0.5 (a false positive that triggers a retrace can regress a clean letter).

detector_suite.name: mask-diff coverage (replaces broken missing_outline_region; font-agnostic backbone)
detector_suite.replaces: outline_issues/missing_outline_region (cascade.py:199; over-fires at every flat cap because a corner sits at sqrt(2)*half-width ~1.41x, exceeding the 1.3x isotropic tolerance by pure geometry)
detector_suite.math: Render the trace back to ink: for each centerline point with half-width r_k stamp a disk; union = reconstructed ink R. MISSING = mask AND NOT dilate(R) (uncovered feature). OVERSHOOT = R AND NOT dilate(mask) (invented ink: stray / overshoot / fork horn). Weight overshoot components by depth-past-ink = max distance_transform_edt(~mask) inside the component, not raw area (a 1px lip is smoothing, a 6px spike is a stray).
detector_suite.algorithm: reconstruct_ink via skimage.draw.disk (vectorised, <50ms/glyph); dilate both sides by aa=1px to absorb the antialiasing band; connected-component the residuals; attribute each to the nearest stroke. THREE non-optional refinements or it fires on every glyph: (1) reconstruct from PRE-taper half-widths (taper deliberately shrinks stroke ends -> false missing at every tip otherwise — note smooth_and_wobble returns pre-taper widths, taper is applied at render time, so use the returned widths directly); (2) depth-weighted overshoot severity; (3) reconstruct from PRE-wobble centerline or set aa >= wobble amplitude. This detector is font-agnostic and grounded in the artist's own MAT width model; its overshoot signal CO-LOCATES with the invented-fork detector, turning the prompt's observed FP-correlation into a clean agreement signal. Retracing adds zero residual (disk union is idempotent) -> correctly blind to legitimate script double_trace.
detector_suite.calibration: Positives = labeled stray(6)+missing_feature; sweep AREA_MIN and DEPTH_MIN to separate smoothing lips (shallow, thin) from real spikes (deep, elongated). GroupKFold-by-font so the threshold measures cross-font transfer.

detector_suite.name: invented_terminal_fork detector (cap-only / object-angle)
detector_suite.replaces: terminal_hook_issues flatness gate (cascade.py:286; fits ALL outline points within 2x width of the end -> a U-shape of both stem flanks + cap, deviation always high, gate never passes)
detector_suite.math: Isolate ONLY the end-cap segment: outline points projecting AHEAD of the terminal tip along the exit tangent (along-tangent coord in [-0.25*hw, 1.0*w]) and within 1.2*half-width perpendicular — this excludes the two stem flanks that made the old fit always-high. Test (a) spine heading turn > turn_deg within 1.5*width AND (b) cap arc is FLAT: PCA max perpendicular deviation <= flat*width AND span >= 0.8*width. Compute exit tangent from a point 1.5w BACK so it reflects the spine, not the hook. Optional cross-check: object/separation angle at the tip via the captured EDT inds field (corner-convergent contacts ~>150deg same-side).
detector_suite.algorithm: A flat cap (low cap deviation) + spine kink = invented fork (HIGH). A real serif's cap points protrude (high deviation) -> not flagged -> preserves approved Garamond flicks. A cursive exit curves smoothly with no flat one-width cap -> not flagged -> preserves script terminals. Keep the detector's discriminator (cap-flatness) DISTINCT from the fix's discriminator (skeleton separation-angle prune) so they fail independently — avoid grading-your-own-homework. After the skeleton fix lands this detector mostly has nothing to fire on; it serves as the regression post-condition.
detector_suite.calibration: Only 14 labeled positives -> wide Wilson intervals; treat as report/monitor not a hard gate. Fit turn_deg (~30-35) and flat (~0.3) on the 14 Lato forks vs approved Garamond serifs. Supersample the mask 2x for the optional object-angle contact computation if pixelation hurts recall (deterministic).

detector_suite.name: topology count-bound + scored convention priors
detector_suite.replaces: spec_issues hard count (cascade.py:220, brittle) for the count side; adds the missing direction/order audit
detector_suite.math: (a) Count bound: instead of exact spec match, flag only when |actual - expected| exceeds a width-derived tolerance OR when stroke count exceeds a topological upper bound (edges + expected terminals) — catches gross over_split without firing on approved +1 flick strokes. (b) Convention priors as signed post-conditions: closed-bowl handedness = sign of shoelace area (CCW expected, negative in y-down); print vertical stem top-down ONLY when the stroke is nearly-straight (heading std < 0.25 rad) AND vertical AND not a script-class entry/exit (ABSTAIN otherwise — cursive upstrokes legitimate); ordering = tiny-stroke-before-main flag, length-gated at 0.25*median.
detector_suite.algorithm: All convention checks emit LOW severity advisories, never trigger auto-retrace. They audit the bowl-CCW sign flip and orientation across all 6 fonts and catch regressions.
detector_suite.calibration: FIRST measure inter-sweep Cohen's kappa per kind on the two sweeps — it is the recall ceiling. If humans disagree on a convention (order is 'a tendency not a law'), DROP that rule from CI rather than encode a contested prior. The bowl-CCW correction inverts any pre-correction labels — relabel or sign-flip before fitting or the detector learns the wrong sign.

implementation_order: 0. PRECONDITION (blocking): verify the 624 per-(font,char) labels are recoverable as a flat ground-truth table. epst_batch_qa.json holds AGGREGATES + ~10 example letters per kind, not 312 per-letter records. If the labeled diagnostic artifacts exist on disk, materialize ground_truth.py (font,char,sweep)->{ok,kinds}; if only aggregates exist, fall back to a stratified ~120-letter relabel with Wilson intervals. Without this, no threshold can be ROC-fitted. Also note epst_batch_qa.json predates the junction-first rewrite, so under_split/double_trace labels are STALE — only over_split, invented_terminal_fork, stray, direction/order are live targets.

1. On-ink clip pass (cleanup_pass). Strict no-op on correct input, cannot regress the 51/52 script path, immediately kills the 6 stray cases. Ship first, re-render 6 fonts, confirm zero stroke-count change on Caveat/DancingScript (the regression tripwire).

2. Detector-suite rewrite (curve_profile + 5 detectors). Touches only quality/ so it cannot change rendered glyphs. Land it BEFORE the tracer fixes so the other fixes can be MEASURED against the labels instead of eyeballed. Calibrate all thresholds here by ROC/GroupKFold-by-font, F-beta=0.5. Freeze a baseline (commit hash + per-kind counts + per-detector held-out precision) into design/detector_baseline.json.

3. EDT index capture + separation-angle skeleton gate (invented_terminal_fork root fix). Highest leverage but highest blast radius. Validate the sep-angle bimodality on Lato first (unit-test _separation_angle on a synthetic rectangle cap -> tip angle small, and a synthetic bracketed serif -> angle high). Re-render; expect Lato l/r/d/F/u/x/N hooks to vanish, Caveat/DancingScript counts IDENTICAL.

4. Stub absorption (residual over_split). Run after build_chains, before orientation. Validate on Arvo X/m/E and EBGaramond H/W — counts should DROP toward spec; confirm approved Garamond flicks survive as attached tails (stroke count drops but the flick is still drawn). Watch Arvo condensed E middle bar for a near-threshold false absorb.

5. Closed-loop CCW sign flip (bowl direction). Pure convention, trivially reversible. Re-render o/a/d/g/b/p/q/e and have vision-QA ratify — only vision can confirm the flip reads as natural. Audit with the bowl-handedness detector across all 6 fonts.
6. _orient_walk_for_writing straightness-abstain (direction prior). Smallest, lowest-risk. Confirm no script-font regression.

Validation gate between every step: `python tests/test_smoke.py` (PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 on Windows) then re-run scripts/batch_google_fonts.py across the 6 fonts and DIFF stroke counts against the frozen baseline. Hard tripwire: Caveat/DancingScript stroke counts must stay identical at every step.
open_questions: Are the 624 per-letter labels actually on disk as a parseable table, or only as the aggregates + example lists in epst_batch_qa.json? This gates the entire calibration methodology and is the literal first action. If absent, the deliverable degrades to a stratified relabel.

What is the inter-sweep Cohen's kappa per issue-kind? It caps achievable detector recall and decides whether the contested convention rules (order, direction) belong in CI at all. Especially: do the two sweeps agree that Garamond H's serif flicks are 'ok'? If humans disagree there, no over_split detector should fire on them.

For the separation-angle gate: does the disc-rim crossing method give a clean bimodal split on real Lato flat caps (~40deg) vs Garamond serifs (~170deg) at 384px after sigma=1.5 boundary smoothing? Needs an isolated unit test before wiring into prune_skeleton. Oblique/italic terminals may land at intermediate angles — is the 2.0x length cap sufficient containment?

Does stub absorption's shared-pixel host-matching hold after merge_nearby_junctions(max_dist=22) — i.e. is the junction pixel that a stub shares with its host still byte-identical in both chains' stored walks, or can merging have shifted one copy? If shifted, _find_host_sharing_node needs a small radius tolerance.

Should the cap-veto in analyze_junctions be built at all, or is the skeleton separation-angle prune sufficient alone? Recommendation: build only the prune first; add the veto only if the post-fix detector still finds residual forks. Do not build both a prune and a post-hoc hook remover.

The mask-diff detector must reconstruct from PRE-taper, PRE-wobble widths/centerline. smooth_and_wobble returns pre-taper widths but post-wobble centerline (wobble_amp=0.18 default). Is the pre-wobble walk available to the cascade, or must QA traces be produced with wobble_amp=0? This affects both mask-diff and all curvature detectors.

Is the CCW bowl direction genuinely universal for this font set's intended hand, including the entry-point choice (rightmost-of-top vs plain topmost)? 'g' double-loops and single-story 'a' may need different entry points; only vision-QA can ratify.

'c' (open arc) direction is deliberately out of scope — does it actually read wrong in the current output, and if so does fixing it in _orient_walk_for_writing risk the legitimate cursive-upstroke-entry cases the user flagged? Defer to a separate vision-validated pass.
